extracted.intended_audience: researchers using or planning to apply for JSPS Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the purpose, scope, and selection principles for Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI); intended to guide researchers who will apply for or manage these competitive research funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose — significant development of scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research are competitive research funds that are intended to significantly develop all scientific research (research based on the free ideas of the researcher), from basic to applied research in all fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targets projects that contribute substantially to the advancement of science across disciplines; applicants should propose work that meaningfully furthers their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator-initiated research (free ideas of the researcher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research based on the free ideas of the researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KAKENHI supports proposals that originate from the researcher’s own ideas rather than top-down mandates; proposals should demonstrate the applicant’s independent conceptualization of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for creative and pioneering research
rubrics_metrics.description: The grants provide financial support for creative and pioneering research projects that will become the foundation of social development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are expected to be innovative or pioneering in approach or topic and to have potential broader societal impact; emphasize novelty and long-term significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — all fields from humanities to natural sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The program covers all fields, ranging from the humanities and the social sciences to the natural sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from any academic discipline are eligible under appropriate research categories; choose the category that matches your field and project aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection mechanism — peer-review screening
rubrics_metrics.description: The research projects are selected using a peer-review screening process (screening by multiple researchers whose field of specialization is close to that of the applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be evaluated by multiple expert reviewers familiar with the applicant’s specialization; clarity, rigor, and fit to reviewers’ expectations are important for favorable assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of dissemination — publication of research results
rubrics_metrics.description: Research results obtained under these Grants-in-Aid are widely published in academic journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded projects are expected to disseminate findings through peer-reviewed publications; applicants should indicate plans for publishing and sharing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple grant categories with specific purposes and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: There are different Types of Grants Programs; refer to 'Types of Grants Programs' for the purposes and description of each research category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must select the appropriate research category (e.g., Specially Promoted Research, Scientific Research (S), Transformative Research Areas) and follow the category-specific purposes, requirements, and application instructions.
